subproblem.title: Mollification of Lipschitz maps: C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz approximants within Λ/(j + 1)
subproblem.statement: For all N, N' ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz map F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there are maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ), each C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) and Λ-Lipschitz, with |F_j(x) − F(x)| ≤ Λ/(j + 1) for all j ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N'), LipschitzWith Λ F → ∃ Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N', (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (Fs j)) ∧ (∀ j, LipschitzWith Λ (Fs j)) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : Euclid N), dist (Fs j x) (F x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof 0(f) (mollification), with σ := 1/(j + 1).
1. Fix j and σ := 1/(j + 1) > 0. Let b : ℝ^N → ℝ be the C^∞ bump function of a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn := σ/2 and rOut := σ (instance hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace): b is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, b(0) = 1, support b = ball(0, σ) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), and b has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport).
2. I := ∫ b > 0: b is continuous with compact support, hence integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport); b ≥ 0; its support ball(0, σ) is a nonempty open set and volume on ℝ^N is positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpenPosMeasure of the additive Haar measure), so integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives I > 0. Put ϕ := I⁻¹·b: C^∞, ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ϕ = 1, support ϕ ⊆ ball(0, σ), compact support.
3. Define F_j(x) := ∫ ϕ(y)·F(x − y) dy, i.e. F_j = ϕ ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ] F (Mathlib convolution with respect to volume). F is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ϕ is C^∞ with compact support, so F_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). For each x the integrand y ↦ ϕ(y)·F(x − y) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
4. Lipschitz bound. For x, x': F_j(x) − F_j(x') = ∫ ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x' − y)) dy, and ‖ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x' − y))‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖. Hence ‖F_j(x) − F_j(x')‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖ dy = Λ‖x − x'‖ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the integrable majorant ϕ·Λ‖x − x'‖). So F_j is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. Distance to F. Since ∫ϕ = 1, F_j(x) − F(x) = ∫ ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x)) dy. For y ∈ support ϕ we have ‖y‖ < σ, so ‖ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x))‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λ‖y‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λσ; for y ∉ support ϕ the integrand is 0. Hence ‖F_j(x) − F(x)‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λσ dy = Λσ = Λ/(j + 1).
6. Steps 1–5 apply verbatim for every N (for N = 0, ℝ^0 is a point, volume is the unit Dirac mass and ball(0, σ) = {0} is open, nonempty and of positive measure; alternatively F_j := F, which is constant, works). □
proof_key_steps: Normalized C^∞ bump ϕ = b/∫b supported in ball(0, 1/(j+1)) (ContDiffBump; ∫b > 0 by positivity on a nonempty open set).
F_j(x) − F_j(x') = ∫ϕ(y)(F(x−y) − F(x'−y)) gives the Lipschitz constant Λ.
F_j(x) − F(x) = ∫ϕ(y)(F(x−y) − F(x)) gives |F_j − F| ≤ Λ/(j+1).

audit.reason: Normalized bump convolution supplies smooth approximants with exactly the stated Lipschitz constant and error rate. Positivity, integrability, and the zero-dimensional case are justified. The proof establishes the quantified statement without another construction or search obligation.
